title: Pre-course setups and requirements
text: Here we explain how to install R and RStudio on your own computer. This is required to ensure a smooth experience and reproducible results during the course.

title: Pre-course setups and requirements
text:
R

Go to the R website
In the column on the left hand side, click on the CRAN link under the subheading Download

You now see a page with CRAN Mirrors. This is a list of servers from which the R software and extensions can be downloaded from

Click on the first link

Now both the left hand side and the right hand side of the page change (This page can be saved as a bookmark/favorite)

On the right hand side, click on the download link for your operating system

E.g. Windows users click on Download R for Windows, then click on base and download the program from there.
It is recommended to install the latest version as well as to upgrade the program if a new major version is released, which is about once per year
You can use the default installation options

title: Pre-course setups and requirements
text:
RStudio Desktop

Go to the download page
Scroll down, look for 2: Install Rstudio and click on the button for downloading RStudio Desktop
Download and install RStudio Desktop

You can use the default installation options

Open Rstudio Desktop, to check that everything has been installed correctly

E.g. via the Start menu in Windows

title: Pre-course setups and requirements
text:
R Packages
Once R and RStudio are installed, you need to install the specific libraries we will use for data visualization and analysis.
Instructions:

Open RStudio.
Copy the code below and paste it into the Console (the bottom-left pane).
Press Enter.

# List of required packages
update.packages()

pkgs <- c("ggplot2", "ggsurvfit", "survminer", "eventglm", "cmprsk")

# Install packages if not installed yet
for (i in pkg) {
  if (i %in% rownames(installed.packages()) == FALSE) {
  install.packages(i, repos = "http://cran.rstudio.com")
}

devtools::install_github("hputter/mstate")

title: Competing Risks and Multi-State Models
text:
We decide which quantity is best suited to answer a specific research question in a setting with competing risks
Understand the concepts of cause-specific hazard, subdistribution hazard and cause-specific cumulative incidence
Be able to choose between a Cox model and a Fine and Gray model
Understand the concepts in multi-state models like transition hazards/intensities, transition probabilities, state occupation probabilities, the Markov assumption
Understand the relation between transition intensities and transition probabilities, and be acquainted with the Aalen-Johansen estimator
Understand how (transition-specific) covariables can be included in proportional hazard models for the transition hazards
Know how to perform the analysis using R
Be able to correctly interpret the results that are obtained.

Welcome to the Course Competing Risks and Multi-State Models. This course is designed to enhance the understanding of competing risks and multi-state models and allow participants to perform such analyses in R. The focus is on applications in medical research.

title: Additional R Resources
text: Welcome! Beyond this medical statistics course, we highly recommend exploring these dedicated R programming resources developed by the OUCRU Math Modelling and Biostatistics groups.

title: Additional R Resources
text:
📚 Training & Community


R Training 2025






Foundational R Skills A comprehensive course covering the essentials of R, from data manipulation with dplyr to professional visualization with ggplot2. Perfect for those who want a solid programming foundation before diving deeper into statistics. Go to Course →





R Cafe Materials






Continuous Learning The “R Cafe” is our community-driven space for sharing tips, advanced tricks, and solving specific coding challenges. These materials include slide decks and scripts from our regular meetups. Browse Materials →







How to use these resources

New to R? Start with the R Training 2025 link to get comfortable with the syntax.
Need specific solutions? Search the R Cafe Materials for localized examples and community-tested code.

If you have questions about any of these materials, feel free to leave a comment below or reach out to the Biostatistics group.
